elaine: Heads up — noticed a ~8% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on canary yesterday after the tool-call metadata change. Spike in tail latency too.
samir: Yikes. Which change exactly? ordering of tool fields?
elaine: PR #4521 reordered function/tool call args to be deterministic (name, args, kwargs, meta). We also rolled tokenizer v1.4.2 -> v1.5.0 in the same deploy.
jun: Do we have a perf profile linking misses to cache key differences or batching behavior?
perf-bot: Profiling summary (canary-2026-03-17):
- total requests sampled: 18k
- prefix cache hit-rate: 68% (baseline 76%)
- median latency: +12ms
- 99th latency: +38ms
- KV cache miss distribution: 63% due to key mismatch, 37% due to eviction
katie: Key mismatch being the majority points to key normalization change rather than eviction policy. Any examples of pairs that mismatch?
elaine: Found a few real examples. Old key: `prompt|system:welcome|toolcalls:[{"id":10}]|tokenizer:1.4.2` New key: `prompt|system:welcome|toolcalls:[{"id":10,"meta":null}]|tokenizer:1.5.0` — tool meta insertion + tokenizer tag changed ordering/content.
mike: So two axes: tokenizer version tag and toolfield normalization. Which one is the primary culprit? Can we isolate with A/B?
samir: I ran a quick split on dev cluster: keep tokenizer v1.4.2 but apply toolfield ordering -> hit-rate drops 3%. Keep tool ordering old but bump tokenizer -> hit-rate drops 5%. Combined -> ~8%. So tokenizer bump bigger but both additive.
jun: Interesting. Why is tokenizer version baked into the key? We pinned it to avoid cross-version tokenization mismatches for cache correctness. But perhaps we can be smarter — only include tokenizer fingerprint when tokenization actually differs for the prompt shape.
katie: Another angle: kernel selection + batching heuristics might amplify perceived latency when miss-rate rises. More misses => more cold KV loads => different kernel path?
elaine: On the kernel side, misses cause additional decoding setup and sometimes trigger an alternate quantized kernel for the uncached prefix. That path has slightly higher per-token overhead which inflates tail latency.
perf-bot: Trace snippet (example request id abc123):
```
prepare_prefix_cache_lookup -> miss
load_prefix_from_s3 -> 62ms
compile_alt_kernel -> 14ms
batching_window_extended -> +10ms
start_generation -> ...
```

mike: Two near-term mitigations: 1) revert tokenizer tag in cache key to previous semantic (or loosen to fingerprint only on token length diff), 2) make toolfield normalization deterministic but compact (collapse null/empty fields). Both could cut mismatch rate.
samir: Agreed. Also propose a warmup-only fastpath: if key mismatch due only to tokenizer tag, attempt secondary lookup by stripping tokenizer tag before doing remote load. That avoids recompile if we find a compatible cached prefix.
jun: That adds extra lookup but only on misses; we should measure false positives. We can cap to short prefixes (<256 tokens) to limit extra work.
elaine: Plan: revert tokenizer tag change on canary for next deploy (owner: samir), push a normalization sanitizer for toolfields to collapse empty meta entries (owner: katie), and prototype a secondary-key lookup warmup (owner: jun). Target: ship fixes today to bring hit-rate back to >=74%.
mike: Also add a regression test to the cachekey suite comparing keys pre/post changes across a corpus of real prompts. Catch tokenizer-normalized diffs and toolfield permutations.
samir: I'll open the revert PR and add a note in changelog. Jun/katie, ping me when you have patches and I’ll coordinate a small canary.
elaine: Thanks. One more request: add an observability flag to measure "secondary-key fallback success" so we can quantify warmup benefit.
perf-bot: Created ticket PERF-9812: measure secondary-key fallback + dashboard panel.
katie: I'll add the cachekey unit tests and a linter rule to forbid inserting explicit nulls into tool meta serialization.
jun: I'll prototype the fallback and can test on dev with a sampled workload.
samir: Cool. If we get hit-rate back, follow-up: evaluate moving tokenizer fingerprinting to a separate namespace so we can TTL independently.
elaine: Great. I'll monitor canary and report back in this thread. :thumbsup:
samir: Thanks all — appreciate the quick triage.
